title: Baked Lemon Herb Salmon with Roasted Vegetables
ingredients: 1 cup baby carrots (or sliced zucchini for variation)
substitutions: For a vegan/vegetarian option, substitute with firm tofu marinated in lemon, garlic, and herbs.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C).
On a large baking sheet lined with parchment paper, arrange the salmon fillets. Drizzle with 1 tbsp olive oil, and sprinkle the minced garlic, lemon zest, dill, salt, and pepper over the fish.
Arrange the vegetables around the salmon; drizzle with the remaining olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and add a few lemon slices for extra flavor.
Bake for about 15–18 minutes until the salmon is opaque and flakes easily, and the vegetables are tender.
Squeeze additional lemon juice over the top before serving.
mealPreppingTip: Roast a batch of vegetables and prepare individual portions of salmon. Store in airtight containers and reheat in a 350°F oven for a few minutes.

title: Easy Chicken Stir‑Fry with Broccoli
ingredients: 1 lb boneless, skinless chicken breast, thinly sliced (or tofu strips for a vegetarian version)
3 tbsp soy sauce (or tamari for gluten‑free)
1 tbsp cornstarch dissolved in 2 tbsp water (optional, for thicker sauce)
substitutions: Use tamari for gluten‑free; substitute chicken with tofu or tempeh for vegetarian options.
instructions: In a large wok or skillet, heat the oil over medium-high heat. Add the chicken slices and stir‑fry until lightly browned and cooked through (about 5–7 minutes). Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.
Add garlic, ginger, onion, broccoli, and red bell pepper to the same pan; stir‑fry for about 3–4 minutes until the vegetables are crisp‑tender.
Return the chicken to the pan. Stir in the soy sauce and honey. If you like a thicker sauce, add the cornstarch mixture and cook for an additional 1–2 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Serve immediately over steamed rice or noodles.
mealPreppingTip: Prepare the stir‑fry and store in individual meal prep containers; reheat in the microwave for 2–3 minutes, and pack steamed rice separately to retain texture.

title: Veggie‑Packed Spaghetti with Tomato Basil Sauce
ingredients: Salt, pepper, and ½ tsp red pepper flakes (optional)
2 tbsp grated Parmesan cheese (or dairy‑free substitute)
substitutions: Use gluten‑free pasta and dairy‑free cheese as needed.
instructions: Cook the spaghetti according to package instructions; drain and set aside.
In a large skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat and sauté the diced onion and garlic until translucent (about 3–4 minutes).
Add the cherry tomatoes and red pepper flakes, and cook for another 5 minutes until the tomatoes soften and create a sauce.
Add the cooked pasta to the skillet, toss to combine, and season with salt and pepper.
Tear in fresh basil leaves and sprinkle Parmesan on top before serving.
mealPreppingTip: Store pasta and sauce together in airtight containers. When reheating, add a splash of water or olive oil to restore moisture.

title:
Slow Cooker 
Beef Stew
ingredients: 1 lb beef stew meat, cubed (or use seitan for a vegetarian version)
3 carrots, peeled and cut into chunks
2 cups beef broth (or vegetable broth for vegetarian)
2 tbsp flour (use gluten‑free flour if needed) for thickening
substitutions: Use gluten‑free flour for thickening; substitute beef with plant‑based protein (like seitan or mushrooms) for a vegetarian option.
instructions: In a skillet, heat olive oil over medium-high heat. Brown the beef cubes on all sides (this enhances flavor).
Transfer the beef to your slow cooker. Add the carrots, celery, onion, garlic, diced tomatoes, thyme, bay leaf, salt, and pepper.
Sprinkle the flour over the ingredients and stir gently to coat.
Pour in the broth, cover, and cook on low for 7–8 hours or on high for 3–4 hours until the meat is tender.
Remove the bay leaf, adjust seasonings, and serve.
mealPreppingTip: Portion the stew into containers; it can be stored in the fridge for up to 4 days or frozen for longer storage.

title: Stuffed Portobello Mushrooms with Quinoa
ingredients: 4 large Portobello mushrooms, stems removed and gills lightly scraped
¼ cup crumbled feta cheese (optional; use dairy‑free cheese for vegan)
Salt, pepper, and 1 tsp Italian seasoning
substitutions: Use a vegan cheese alternative or omit the cheese for a dairy‑free version.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a bowl, combine cooked quinoa, spinach, diced tomatoes, garlic, Italian seasoning, and half of the olive oil. Season with salt and pepper.
Place the Portobello mushrooms on a baking dish (gill side up) and spoon the quinoa mixture evenly into each cap.
Top with crumbled feta cheese, drizzle with the remaining olive oil, and bake for 18–20 minutes until the mushrooms are tender.
Serve warm.
mealPreppingTip: Prepare the stuffed mushrooms ahead and reheat individually in the oven or microwave for a quick dinner.

title: Mediterranean Chicken with Olives and Tomatoes
ingredients: ½ cup Kalamata olives, pitted and halved
substitutions: For a vegetarian option, swap chicken with hearty eggplant slices.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a bowl, combine the olive oil, garlic, oregano, lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Toss the chicken thighs in the marinade.
Arrange the chicken in a baking dish with cherry tomatoes, olives, and red onion slices.
Bake for 25–30 minutes until the chicken is fully cooked and the vegetables are tender.
Serve with a side of whole‑grain bread or over rice.
mealPreppingTip: Prepare the dish in a larger baking tray; store leftovers in containers for a balanced, ready‑to‑reheat dinner.

title: Vegan Chickpea Curry with Spinach
ingredients: 1 cup coconut milk (or use oat milk if allergic to coconut)
2 tbsp coconut oil or olive oil
substitutions: Use oat or almond milk (if nut allergies aren’t a concern) for a creamier base.
instructions: In a large pot, heat the oil over medium heat. Sauté the chopped onion until translucent (about 3–4 minutes).
Add garlic, ginger, curry powder, and turmeric; cook for another minute until fragrant.
Stir in chickpeas and diced tomatoes along with their juices. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk, bring to a gentle simmer, and cook for 10 minutes.
Fold in the fresh spinach until wilted; season with salt and pepper.
Serve hot over steamed rice or quinoa.
mealPreppingTip: Divide into mason jars or containers. This curry tastes even better the next day as flavors meld.

title: Pesto Zoodle Pasta with Grilled Chicken or Tofu
ingredients: 1 cup fresh basil pesto (use dairy‑free pesto for vegan, or homemade basil blend without cheese)
2 grilled chicken breasts, sliced or 1 block firm tofu (pressed and cubed)
substitutions: Use dairy‑free pesto and ensure tofu is prepared for vegan options.
instructions: Spiralize the zucchinis into noodles (“zoodles”) using a spiralizer or vegetable peeler.
In a large bowl, toss the zoodles with the pesto and a drizzle of olive oil; season with salt and pepper.
Top with sliced grilled chicken or tofu cubes, and add cherry tomatoes for brightness.
Serve immediately or chill for a cold, refreshing meal.
mealPreppingTip: Keep the pesto separate until serving to avoid soggy zoodles. Pack chicken or tofu ahead for quick assembly.

title: Creamy Shrimp & Broccoli Alfredo
ingredients: 1 lb shrimp, peeled and deveined (or use a plant‑based alternative such as tempeh)
1 cup heavy cream (or coconut cream for a dairy‑free version)
½ cup grated Parmesan cheese (or dairy‑free substitute)
Salt, pepper, and ½ tsp Italian seasoning
substitutions: Use gluten‑free pasta, dairy‑free cream cheese or coconut cream, and omit shrimp for a vegetarian version.
instructions: Cook the pasta according to package directions; set aside and keep warm.
In a large pan, melt butter over medium heat; add garlic and sauté for 1 minute.
Add the shrimp and cook until pink and opaque (about 2–3 minutes per side). Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, add broccoli and a splash of water; cover and steam for 3–4 minutes until tender-crisp.
Pour in the heavy cream and stir in Parmesan, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper. Let simmer for 3 minutes until slightly thickened.
Return the shrimp to the pan and toss with the pasta until evenly coated.
Serve immediately, garnished with extra Parmesan if desired.
mealPreppingTip: Pack pasta and sauce separately; reheat on the stovetop with a splash of water, then combine with freshly cooked or reheated broccoli and shrimp.

title: Vegetarian Stuffed Bell Peppers
ingredients: 4 bell peppers (any color), tops sliced off and seeds removed
1 cup cooked brown rice or quinoa
1 can black beans, rinsed and drained
1 tsp cumin and ½ tsp chili powder
½ cup shredded cheese (or vegan cheese alternative)
substitutions: Use a dairy‑free cheese for a vegan version.
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a bowl, mix together rice/quinoa, black beans, corn, diced tomatoes, cumin, chili powder, salt, and pepper.
Stuff each bell pepper with the mixture; top with shredded cheese.
Place stuffed peppers in a baking dish, drizzle with olive oil, cover with foil, and bake for 30 minutes. Remove foil and bake an additional 10 minutes until peppers are tender and cheese is melted.
Serve warm.
mealPreppingTip: Prepare the filling ahead; assemble and bake when ready. Leftovers reheat well in the microwave.

title: One‑Pan Chicken and Veggies Bake
ingredients: 4 chicken thighs or breasts (bone‑in or boneless as preferred)
substitutions: For a vegetarian version, substitute chicken with tempeh or marinated tofu.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a large bowl, combine all vegetables and garlic with olive oil, rosemary, salt, and pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
Arrange the chicken and vegetables on a large baking sheet in a single layer.
Roast for 35–40 minutes until chicken is cooked through and vegetables are tender, stirring once halfway through.
Serve directly from the pan or transfer to serving dishes.
mealPreppingTip: Portion leftovers into containers for an easy reheat. The dish improves in flavor the next day.

title: Crispy Baked Tofu with Peanut Sauce
ingredients: 1 block extra‑firm tofu, pressed and cubed
2 tbsp soy sauce (or tamari for gluten‑free)
For the Peanut Sauce: 3 tbsp natural peanut butter (or sunflower seed butter for nut allergies), 2 tbsp soy sauce/tamari, 1 tbsp maple syrup, 1 tsp rice vinegar, water to thin
substitutions: Use sunflower seed butter for nut allergies and tamari for gluten‑free.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss tofu cubes with soy sauce and then gently coat with cornstarch. Arrange on a baking sheet and bake for 25–30 minutes until crispy, flipping halfway through.
Meanwhile, prepare the peanut sauce by whisking together peanut butter, soy sauce, maple syrup, rice vinegar, and water until smooth.
In a skillet, heat vegetable oil over medium heat. Sauté bok choy and red bell pepper until just tender (about 3–4 minutes).
Serve the crispy tofu over the vegetables, drizzled with the peanut sauce.
mealPreppingTip: Prepare extra tofu and sauce in advance. Store the sautéed vegetables separately and combine when reheating.

title:
Roasted Eggplant 
Parmesan
ingredients: 1 large eggplant, sliced into ½‑inch rounds
1 cup shredded mozzarella cheese (or dairy‑free alternative)
½ cup grated Parmesan (or nutritional yeast for a vegan option)
1 tsp dried basil and oregano blend
2 eggs, beaten (or flax egg for vegan)
substitutions: Use dairy‑free cheese, a flax egg, and gluten‑free breadcrumbs for a vegan/gluten‑free version.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). Season eggplant slices with salt and let them sit for 10 minutes; pat dry.
Dip each slice in beaten egg (or flax egg), then coat with a mixture of breadcrumbs, basil, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Place slices on a lightly greased baking sheet, spray with olive oil, and bake for 25 minutes until golden.
Spoon marinara sauce over each eggplant slice, sprinkle with mozzarella and Parmesan (or substitutes), and bake uncovered for an additional 10 minutes until cheese is melted and bubbly.
mealPreppingTip: Assemble the eggplant Parmesan in a baking dish; refrigerate and reheat in the oven for a comforting dinner.

title: Coconut Lime Chicken Curry
ingredients: 1 lb chicken breast, cut into cubes (or jackfruit for a vegan alternative)
1 can coconut milk (or use dairy‑free cream alternative if allergic to coconut)
substitutions: Use an alternative dairy‑free milk such as oat or cashew milk if coconut is an issue (adjust thickness with a bit of cornstarch if needed).
instructions: In a large pan, heat vegetable oil over medium heat and sauté the onion until softened.
Add garlic, ginger, and curry powder; cook for 1–2 minutes until aromatic.
Stir in chicken cubes and cook until lightly browned.
Add red bell pepper and coconut milk. Bring to a simmer and cook for 15–20 minutes until chicken is cooked through and the sauce has thickened slightly.
Stir in lime juice and zest; adjust seasonings with salt and pepper. Garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.
mealPreppingTip: Store in portioned containers and serve over rice or quinoa. The flavors deepen after a day in the fridge.

title: Beef and Broccoli with Brown Rice
ingredients: 1 lb flank or sirloin steak, thinly sliced against the grain (or use seitan strips for a vegetarian option)
2 tbsp soy sauce (or tamari for gluten‑free)
1 tsp cornstarch dissolved in 2 tbsp water
substitutions: Use tamari and gluten‑free oyster sauce or simply omit it. For a vegetarian version, substitute steak with seitan or mushrooms.
instructions: In a wok or large skillet, heat vegetable oil over high heat. Sauté the steak until just browned and remove from the pan.
Add garlic and broccoli; stir‑fry for 3–4 minutes until broccoli is bright green and crisp‑tender.
Return the steak to the pan and stir in soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), and the cornstarch mixture.
Cook for an additional 2 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Serve the beef and broccoli over a bed of warm brown rice.
mealPreppingTip: Portion the rice and stir‑fry separately in microwave‑safe containers; reheat thoroughly before eating.

title: Hearty Lentil Bolognese over Pasta
ingredients: 8 oz pasta (regular, whole grain, or gluten‑free)
instructions: In a pot, heat olive oil over medium heat. Sauté onion, garlic, carrots, and celery until soft (about 5–7 minutes).
Add lentils, diced tomatoes, vegetable broth, oregano, and basil. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and let simmer for 25–30 minutes until the lentils are tender.
Season with salt and pepper. Meanwhile, cook the pasta as directed.
Serve the lentil Bolognese over pasta, with additional herbs or a sprinkle of dairy‑free cheese if desired.
mealPreppingTip: This dish freezes well in individual portions and can be quickly reheated on the stovetop or in the microwave.

title: Grilled Portobello Burger with Avocado Spread
ingredients: 4 large Portobello mushroom caps, stems removed
Lettuce, tomato slices, and red onion for garnish
substitutions: Use gluten‑free buns; the avocado spread may be swapped for hummus if preferred.
instructions: In a bowl, whisk together balsamic vinegar, olive oil, garlic, salt, and pepper. Brush the Portobello caps on both sides with the marinade.
Preheat a grill or grill pan over medium-high heat; grill the mushrooms for 4–5 minutes per side until tender and juicy.
Toast the burger buns lightly.
Assemble each burger with a grilled Portobello cap, a generous spread of mashed avocado, and desired garnishes such as lettuce, tomato, and onion slices.
Serve with a side salad or baked sweet potato fries.
mealPreppingTip: Marinate the mushrooms ahead of time and store them in the refrigerator. Assemble burgers fresh to avoid sogginess.

title: Creamy Cauliflower Soup with Garlic Croutons
ingredients: 1 medium head cauliflower, cut into florets
For Croutons: 2 slices bread (or gluten‑free bread), cubed; 1 tbsp olive oil; 1 garlic clove, minced; salt and dried herbs (optional)
substitutions: Use dairy‑free milk and gluten‑free bread for croutons.
instructions: In a large pot, heat olive oil over medium heat and sauté onion and garlic until soft (about 5 minutes).
Add cauliflower florets and vegetable broth; bring to a simmer and cook until the cauliflower is very tender (about 15 minutes).
Use an immersion blender (or transfer in batches) to blend the soup until smooth.
Stir in the milk and adjust seasonings with salt and pepper; gently reheat if necessary.
For the croutons, toss bread cubes with olive oil, minced garlic, salt, and herbs. Toast in the oven at 375°F (190°C) for 10 minutes until crispy.
Serve the soup topped with garlic croutons.
mealPreppingTip: The soup stores well in the refrigerator for up to 4 days. Reheat on the stovetop and add freshly made croutons right before eating.
